MAFIJUL SK ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant-State
of West Bengal. None has appeared for the respondent
accused, though served.
3. Appellant-State of West Bengal is aggrieved by order
dated 25.07.2025, passed by the High Court of Calcutta,
(briefly the ‘High Court’ hereinafter) granting regular
bail to the respondent. Respondent is an accused in
Khargram Police Station Case No.231 of 2023, registered
under Sections 364, 302 and 120B of the Indian Penal
Code, 1860 (IPC).
4. It is a case of kidnapping and subsequent murder of
the husband of the informant. The High Court noticed that
1

--- Page 426 ---
on the date of the passing of the impugned order,
appellant  had  already  undergone  incarceration  for  a
period of one year and six months. After noticing that a
few of the co-accused were granted anticipatory bail, the
High Court allowed the prayer of the respondent for
regular  bail.  While  granting  bail,  the  High  Court
directed  that  respondent  should  remain  within  the
jurisdiction of the Trial Court and shall furnish his
address to the Trial Court, Investigating Officer (IO)
and  the  Officer-in-Charge  of  the  concerned  police
station. He was also directed to provide his mobile
number to the concerned authorities and not to change the
same without prior intimation. Further direction was that
that he should appear on each and every date fixed by the
Trial Court and should not intimidate witnesses or tamper
with the evidence. In the event of any breach of the
conditions, liberty was granted to the Trial Court to
cancel the bail of the respondent.
5. In the hearing today, learned State counsel submits
that out of 13 prosecution witnesses, 3 prosecution
witnesses have been examined. In such circumstances and
further considering the fact that bail was granted to the
respondent more than a year back, we are not inclined to
interfere with the same. However, we request the Trial
Court to expedite the trial and to complete the same
within a period of six months from today.
6. Subject to the above, appeal is disposed of.

Court for onward information of the Trial Court.

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. In these petitions, the submission on behalf of the
petitioners is that the State had wrongly provided vertical
instead  of  horizontal  reservation  to  women  category;
therefore, writ petition(s) were filed before the High
Court by number of candidates. The lead writ petition
titled as M.  Satheesh  Kumar  vs.  State  of  Tamil  Nadu  and
others came to be decided  vide order dated 07.09.2022
wherein, in paragraph 38, the High Court had observed that
2

--- Page 439 ---
the respondents shall re-arrange the entire list as per the
illustration given by this Court in the case of Anil Kumar
Gupta. It is urged that the specific direction to re-
arrange the entire list in terms of this Court’s decision
in Anil Kumar Gupta  would render the decision in rem  and,
therefore, the benefit of that decision must follow to all
participants in the recruitment exercise.
2. The grievance of the petitioner(s) is that the list
was not re-drawn as directed, and when the petitioner(s)
had expressed their grievance later through separate writ
petition(s), their writ petition(s) have been dismissed on
ground of latches by treating the earlier judgment as
limited to the petitioner(s) of that case.
3. Our attention has been drawn to paragraph 38 of the
judgment in  M.  Satheesh  Kumar  (supra)  wherein the High
Court had observed that though it would not be appropriate
to nullify the appointments already made but, at the same
time, it would not be appropriate to deny the right of
appointment to those who were entitled to such appointment
in the order of merit. It has been submitted that even if
the appointment(s) already made are not disturbed, there
are sufficient vacancies against which the petitioner(s)
can  be  accommodated  if  horizontal  reservation,  as
illustrated by this Court in Anil Kumar Gupta, is properly
applied and list is re-drawn on merit.
4. Issue notice, returnable in six weeks.
5. The State in its response shall also provide a chart
3

--- Page 440 ---
indicating the number of posts advertised and the number of
appointment(s) made so far against those advertised posts.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.1172/2012
CHEIF GENERAL MANAGER, BSNL  APPELLANT
                                VERSUS
COLLECTOR OF CENTRAL EXCISE, BHOPAL RESPONDENTS
O R D E R
1. The issues involved in this appeal relates to classification
of the product steel tubular transmission poles (Hamilton poles or
tubes) manufactured by Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (for short
“BSNL”) for the purpose of levy of Central Excise Duty, namely,
whether  the  goods  are  classifiable  under  heading  7308.90
(structures / parts of structures, eligible for exemption) or
under heading 7306.90 (tubes and pipes). Same is no more  res
integra in view of the law laid down by this Court in the matter
of India Metals and Ferro Alloys Ltd., Cuttack Vs. Collector of
Central Excise, Bhubaneswar, 1991 Supp (1) SCC 125.
2. However, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant, by
drawing our attention to the circular No.A-28/1990 dated 27.09.1990
at Annexure-A1 would contend that the goods in question was
classified under sub-heading 7308.90, which was later changed by
circular  dated  06.09.2000  vide  Circular  No.545/41/2000-CX  at
Annexure-A5. As such, the levy for the month of July and August,
2000  would  amount  to  retrospective  application,  which  is
impermissible, and this fact has not been considered by the
1

--- Page 450 ---
authorities as well as by the Appellate Tribunal, namely, CESTAT.
Hence, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant has prayed
for same being set aside and levy being quashed, at least for the
months of July and August, 2000.
3. Per contra , Mr.  Raghavendra P Shankar , learned Additional
Solicitor General of India appearing for the respondent, would
support the impugned order and contends that the show cause notice
itself is of the year 2001, and by circular dated 06.09.2000, the
department has only reiterated the law laid down by this Court in
India Metals and Ferro Alloys Ltd., Cuttack  referred to supra.
Hence, the question of retrospectivity would not arise.
4. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the parties,
and on perusal of the records, we are of the considered view that
the contention raised by the learned counsel appearing for the
appellant does not hold water.
5. A perusal of the show cause notice dated 25.07.2001 would
clearly indicate that it is issued subsequent to the circular dated
06.09.2000, and even in the said circular, what has been stated is
reiteration of the law laid down by this Court, namely, the goods
in question is classifiable under the sub-heading 7306.90 and not
under  7308.90.  As  such,  the  question  of  the  levy  being
retrospectively being applied does not arise.
6. Even otherwise also, it can be noticed that this Court in the
above-referred judgment has clearly held that the goods in question
is classifiable under the sub-heading 7306.90, which judgment came
to be rendered on 22.11.1990 and as such, the show cause notice
issued on 25.07.2001 relating to levy for the period of July and
2

--- Page 451 ---
August, 2000 cannot be construed or held as being retrospectively.
In that view of the matter also, we are of the considered view that
there is no merit in this appeal. Accordingly, it stands dismissed.
7. Pending applications, if any, stands disposed of. Costs made
easy.
.................J.
  (ARAVIND KUMAR)
.................J.
(VIPUL M. PANCHOLI)
NEW DELHI;
JULY 16, 2026.

1.  The petitioner before this Court has filed this
present special leave petition for grant of anticipatory
bail for apprehending his arrest in connection with FIR
No.385  dated  11.09.2024  registered  at  Police  Station
Jagarnathpur, Ranchi. The contention of the petitioner is
that the agreement was executed between the parties in the
year 2018 and in the year 2024 an FIR has been lodged for
offences punishable under Section 406, 420, 504, 506 and 34
of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3(1)(r) of the
Scheduled  Caste  and  Scheduled  Tribe  (Prevention  of
Atrocities) Act, 1989.
2.  Learned counsel for the petitioner has stated that
the petitioner was being harassed by the respondent No.2
alleging that she is one of the family member and land
belongs to her also. The petitioner has lodged a complaint
case against the respondent No.2 and it was only after
receiving summons in the complaint case an FIR has been
lodged against the petitioner.
3.  In the present case, this Court has granted interim
protection to the petitioner on 13.04.2026 and it is
informed by learned counsel for the respondent No.1-State
that the petitioner is co-operating in the investigation.
4.  Learned  counsel  for  the  respondent  No.2  has
vehemently argued before this Court in the present case a
tribal lady has been duped by the petitioner and she has

3
not received money though she is one of the family member
and therefore, the question of grant of anticipatory bail
does not arise.

documents on record is of the opinion that that the interim
order dated 13.04.2026 passed by this Court deserves to be
made absolute and it is made absolute accordingly.
6.  This Court has not observed anything on the merits
of the case, and the parties shall also be free to take

for the respondent-State.

at Tembhurni Police Station, District-Solapur,
Maharashtra, for the offences punishable under
Sections 180 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita, 2023 (for short, ‘the BNS’).

1 SLP(CRL.)NO.15288/2026

submits that the appellant has been in custody
since 20.08.2024, i.e., for more than two years.
5. It is not in dispute that some of the co-accused

incarceration undergone by the appellant, we are
inclined to set aside the impugned order dated

bail to the appellant.

and the appellant is granted bail, subject to
the terms and conditions that can be imposed by
the Trial Court.

inclined to enlarge the petitioners on bail.

1  (2014) 8 SCC 273

--- Page 559 ---
2
3. Learned  Counsel  for  the  petitioner  alertly
pointed out Paragraph 11.7 in the aforesaid judgment,
which enables the High Court to take cognizance of any
contempt committed of the directions issued by this
Court in the cited decision. The grievance is also that
the petitioner was arrested without service of notice
under Section 41A of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973.
4. On the brief facts, we would only look at the
very  complaint  filed  by  the  petitioner,  which  is

is that he was summoned to the Police Station on

till 9 p.m. when he was asked to leave. Anyway, no

that it was on summons that he went to the Police
Station voluntarily. His arrest was on 15.08.2024, when
the Investigating Officer added Section 111(7) of the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 2, wherein the specified
offence of Organized Crime speaks of imprisonment of
not  less  than  3  years,  but  which  may  extend  to
imprisonment for life. 
5. On 15.08.2024, though, initially offences were
alleged under the BNS punishable with imprisonment of
less than 7 years, by adding Section 111(7) of the BNS,
the arrest was justified prima facie.
6. We find absolutely no reason for the High Court
2  In short ‘BNS’

--- Page 560 ---
3
to have initiated contempt proceedings, however, if the
petitioner has any contention against the allegations

               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) Diary No. 35502/2026
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 05-04-2024
in CMA No. 1253/2022 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Madras]
SIVAGAMI & ANR.                                    Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
RELIANCE GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD & ANR.          Respondent(s)
IA No. 297709/2026 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN FILING
IA No. 297704/2026 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN REFILING /  CURING THE
DEFECTS
 
Date : 05-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UJJAL BHUYAN
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ATUL S. CHANDURKAR
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. T. Harish Kumar- 1418, AOR
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the view taken
by the High Court is not supported by a recent decision of this
Court in Wakia Afrin vs. National Insurance Company Limited,  (2026)
3 SCC 418, para 17 of which reads thus:
Trite is the principle that the liability
with  respect  to  an  accident  is  on  the
tortfeasor  and  in  the  case  of  a  motor
vehicle accident if the tortfeasor is the
driver,  the  owner  has  the  vicarious
1

--- Page 562 ---
liability, which liability is indemnified by
the insurer, when there is a valid policy.
The liability is essentially of the owner
but  the  provision,  in  addition  to  the
insured/owner makes liable the authorised
insurer too. Hence, when there is a valid
policy issued in the name of the vehicle
involved in the accident, a claim under
Section 163-A, as per the words employed in
the provision, according to us covers every
claim and is not restricted to a third-party
claim;  without  any  requirement  of
establishing the negligence, if death or
permanent disability is caused by reason of
the motor accident. This would also take in
the liability with respect to the death of
an owner or a driver who stepped into the
shoes of the owner, if the claim is made
under Section 163-A  dehors the statutory
liability  under  Section  147  or  the
contractual liability as reduced to writing
in an insurance policy. It would override
the provisions under Sections 147 and 149
along with the other provisions of the MV
Act and the law regulating insurance as also
the terms of the policy confining the claim
with respect to an owner-driver to a fixed
sum. This according to us is the intention
of incorporating the non obstante clause
under Section 163-A providing for no-fault
liability claims, the compensation for which
is  restricted  to  the  structured  formula
under  the  Second  Schedule.  It  is  a
beneficial piece of legislation brought in,
keeping in mind the enhanced chances of an
2

--- Page 563 ---
accident, resulting from the prevalence of
vehicles in the overcrowded roads of today.
It was a social security scheme, brought
about  considering  the  need  for  a  more
comprehensive scheme of "no-fault" liability
for reason of the ever-increasing instances
of  motor  vehicle  accidents  and  the
difficulty in proving rash and negligent
driving. 
3. Issue notice, returnable on 30.11.2026.
 (IRAMNAZ)                                       (CHETNA BALOONI)
COURT MASTER (SH)                                COURT MASTER (NSH)

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners.
2. The order impugned in these petitions is an interim order
where under the High Court has restrained the petitioners from
paying salaries to the private respondents in the writ petitions
1

--- Page 610 ---
pending before the High Court.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that as on
date there are no recruitment rules notified as they are awaiting
assent of the Governor and, therefore, to meet the administrative
exigencies, the Council had been making ad-hoc arrangements and
those who continued to serve long have been regularized.
4. The High Court while passing the impugned order had been prima
facie of  the  opinion  that  the  Council  had  made  backdoor
appointments without following a transparent recruitment procedure
and, therefore, it deemed it appropriate to restraint the first and
second respondents, namely, the petitioners here, from paying
salaries to the private respondents in the writ petitions pending
before the High Court.
5. The grievance of the petitioners is that if the payment of
salary to its workers is stopped, no worker would render service
and, therefore, the functioning of the Council would come to a
halt. In such circumstances, it has been submitted that the order
passed by the High Court requires modification.
6. Having regard to the submissions made, we are of the view that
the petitioners may move an application before the High Court
seeking modification of the order dated 13.08.2026 so as to enable
the Council to make ad-hoc engagements for the purposes of carrying
out its functions.
7. Accordingly, we deem it appropriate to dispose of these
special leave petitions by giving liberty to the petitioners to
move modification application before the High Court. If any such
application is moved, the High Court shall accord due consideration
2

--- Page 611 ---
to the application and till regular selections are made, the
petitioners may be allowed by the High Court to make ad-hoc
engagements for its functioning.
8. With the aforesaid liberty and observations, these special
leave petitions stand disposed of.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(CHETAN ARORA)                                  (SAPNA BANSAL)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        COURT MASTER (NSH)

dated 07.08.2025 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh
at Jabalpur in Criminal Appeal No.876 of 2025, whereby the
High Court awarded to the appellant sentence of 10 years’
rigorous imprisonment for the offence punishable under
PETITION(S) FOR SPECIAL LEAVE TO APPEAL (CRL.)  NO(S).12559/2026

--- Page 632 ---
2
Section 304 Part I of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for
short, “IPC”), with a fine of Rs. 5,000/-, with a default
stipulation of 06 months rigorous imprisonment. The High
Court while deciding the appeal has also observed that the
incidence was spontaneous, lacked of premeditation and
occurred due to sudden and grave provocation initiated by
the deceased. In the present case, the deceased died on
account of single blow by knife.
4.  Learned counsel for the appellant has argued before
this Court that the appellant has completed four and half
year of sentence out of the 10 years rigorous imprisonment
for the offence punishable under Section 304 Part I of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, “IPC”), with a fine of
Rs.5,000/-. There is no appearance on the other side
inspite of service of notice.
5.  This court after hearing learned counsel for the
appellant is of the opinion that the prayer for suspension
of sentence deserves to be allowed and it is accordingly
allowed, subject to deposit of fine of Rs.5,000/- awarded
by the High Court.
6.  The appellant is accordingly directed to be released
on bail during the pendency of the appeal, subject to such
terms and conditions as may be imposed by the Trial Court.

Section 304 Part I of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for

stipulation of 06 months rigorous imprisonment. The High
Court while deciding the appeal has also observed that the
incidence was spontaneous, lacked of premeditation and

inspite of service of notice.

of sentence deserves to be allowed and it is accordingly
allowed, subject to deposit of fine of Rs.5,000/- awarded
by the High Court.

terms and conditions as may be imposed by the Trial Court.

   UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                         O R D E R
1. We have heard Dr. Menaka Guruswamy, learned senior counsel
appearing for the petitioners, and Mr. Tushar Mehta, learned
Solicitor General appearing for the respondent(s), and considered
the matter in detail.

--- Page 808 ---
2
2. The results of the NEET-UG Examination were declared on
16.07.2026. Thereafter the counseling for the 2 nd round has been
held from 3rd to 11th September, 2026 and even for the 3 rd round from
22nd to  30 th September,  2026.  The  classes  commenced  from  15 th
September, 2026. Therefore, we are of the opinion that the EWS
Certificate obtained by the petitioner(s) after the declaration of
the result, between 20.07.2026 to 15.08.2026 cannot be a ground to
permit them to participate in the counseling as EWS candidates,
particularly when they applied either in the General category or
the OBC category.
3. We express no opinion on the merits of the matter.  However,
the  benefit  of  EWS  will  certainly  enure  in  favour  of  the
petitioners for the next year.  If there is a possibility of
accommodating the EWS candidates, the respondents may consider the
same at the appropriate stage.  
4. With  this  clarification,  the  Special  Leave  Petition  is
disposed of.
5. Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, is/are disposed
of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have perused the report forwarded by the Consultant Nephrologist
attached to Wisdom Superspeciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Pune.
2. It appears that the condition of the petitioner is worsening day by day; his
kidney functioning level has reduced from 16%, as earlier reported, to 11%.
Apart from that, he is also suffering from other ailments and is presently not in a
position to be moved out of hospital.
3. Considering such report, we direct that the petitioner may not be required
to  surrender  unless  his  condition  improves  and  he  is  discharged  from  the
hospital. As and when the petitioner recovers and is on the verge of being
discharged, the hospital shall place a further report before this Court and await
orders before permitting discharge.
4. In the event that, for further treatment, the petitioner is required to be
shifted to any hospital in any other part of the country, the petitioner shall be at
liberty to apply together with the relevant medical report.

developments.

SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) Diary No.52950/2026
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated  12-05-2026
in CM No. 8/2026 passed by the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at
Chandigarh]
M/S LUCKY POULTRY FARM & ANR.                      Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
M/S SAMPOORNA FEEDS PRIVATE LTD.                   Respondent(s)
(IA No. 296625/2026 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN FILING SLP AND IA
No. 296624/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED
JUDGMENT)
 
Date : 05-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE J.B. PARDIWALA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. VINOD CHANDRAN
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Mr. Sanjeev Duggal, Adv.
                   Mr. Harshit Khanduja, Adv.
                   Mr. Pulkit Khanduja, Adv.
                   Mr. Vasu Pandit, Adv.
                   Mr. Sriram P.- 2550, AOR
                   Mr. Ramavath Balaji Naik, Adv.                  
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Exemption Application is allowed.
3. The impugned Order dealt with an application for stay in an
appeal against a money decree. The High Court noted Order XLI Rule
5 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (for short, ‘CPC’) and
apprised the appellants of the requirement to secure the amounts
decreed on the last posting date. When the matter was posted again,
the appellants’ counsel expressed his inability to make any deposit
of money but offered a bank guarantee for a portion of the money

--- Page 980 ---
2
decree. The High Court then refused the interim prayer of stay of
decree.
4. The High Court need not have taken the consent of the
appellants to pass an order securing the amounts shown in the
decree and even when they expressed their inability to deposit any
money or furnish bank guarantee of entire amounts, the High Court
was well within its powers to make an order, the non-compliance of
which would result in the order remaining unenforceable.
5. We are of the opinion that the matter can be settled even
without issuing notice to the respondent since in the nature of the
orders passed, no prejudice would be caused to the respondent.
6. The petitioners’ counsel before us undertook that he would
furnish a bank guarantee securing the entire decretal amount and
interest upto the date of bank guarantee. We pass an order of stay
of the decree in Civil Suit No.1 of 2022 passed by the Additional
District Judge-I, Kapurthala, on condition of furnishing bank
guarantee of the decretal amount together with interest upto the
date of bank guarantee before the High Court within a period of
four weeks from today. There shall be an interim stay of the decree
till the running bank guarantee is furnished and if the bank
guarantee is furnished, the stay shall continue till the appeal is
disposed of. However, on failure to furnish the bank guarantee as
directed herein on refusal at any point of time to revalidate the
bank guarantee, while the appeal is pending, the stay shall stand
vacated and the plaintiff would be entitled to pursue execution of
the decree. 
7. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of with the above
directions.
8. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                                 COURT MASTER (NSH)

Date : 05-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE J.B. PARDIWALA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. VINOD CHANDRAN
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Mr. Ramjee Pandey- 2376, AOR
                   Ms. Sania Khan, Adv.
                   Mr. Praphul Kumar Vohra, Adv.
                   Mr. Yogendra Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Vinay Kumar Sharma, Adv.                   
For Respondent(s) : 
                   Mr. Adarsh Upadhyay- 1776, AOR
                   Ms. Pallavi Kumari, Adv.
                   Mr. Shashank Pachauri, Adv.                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We cannot approve the grounds on which bail has been granted
by the High Court in the impugned judgment. The High Court points
out that the appeal is of the year 2008 and the High Court is
hearing appeals of the year 1983-84 onwards on a priority basis, on
the direction of this Court to decide the oldest appeals first. The
Court also observes that there are 100 appeals listed before the
Court every day, and it is not humanly possible to decide all of it
on merits. In fact, it would have been more appropriate for the
High  Court  to  have  dealt  with  the  suspension  of  sentence

--- Page 982 ---
2
application in a more objective manner in the time it took to make
the above observations; looking into the facts and either allowing
or rejecting the bail on a  prima  facie  consideration of the
material proffered in evidence.
2. Be that as it may, we on the last occasion directed the
parties to place on record the judgment of conviction as passed by
the Additional Sessions Judge (Fast Track Court No.1) Fatehpur
(U.P.) in Sessions Trial No.792 of 2001. The conviction was under
Section 302 read with Section 149 and Sections 144 and 148 of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC). The Court has also handed down a
sentence of life imprisonment with appropriate fine and default
sentence. Having gone through the judgment entering conviction, we
are of the prima facie  opinion that the Respondent No.2 should be
released on bail to facilitate which we suspend the sentence handed
down by the Trial Court in Sessions Trial No.792 of 2001. We notice
the allegation insofar as the cancellation of bail effected by the
High Court at the earlier instance for reason of commission of a
subsequent offence by the Respondent No.2 while on bail. The
Respondent No.2 also has 21 criminal antecedents. Despite this, we
are convinced on a reading of the judgment that in the present case
there is no reason to continue the incarceration of the Respondent
No.2.
3. However, we make it clear that if there is one more commission
of any offence by the Respondent No.2, he shall be immediately
taken into custody and then he shall serve the life sentence
ordered by the Trial Court unless in appeal the same is upset.
4. With the above observation, the grant of bail by the High
Court in the impugned judgment is upheld, for the separate reasons
supplied by us.
5. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand rejected.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                                 COURT MASTER (NSH)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard.
2. The non-compliance of the order passed in W.P. (C) No.22790/2014 dated
30.11.2017 which came to be affirmed by the Division Bench on 15.01.2020 and
Special Leave Petition (Civil) Nos.9529-9534/2018 challenging the said orders
came to be dismissed on 29.01.2021 as also the Review Petition being
dismissed on 21.10.2021, there was non-compliance. Hence, the petitioner
initiated contempt proceedings before the jurisdictional High Court in Contempt
Case (C) No.623/2021 before the jurisdictional High Court. However, an
application came to be filed in being C.M. Application No.1/2025 seeking for
extension of the order for the reasons assigned therein. The High Court not
1

--- Page 1098 ---
being satisfied with the cause for delay being shown still extended the olive
branch by granting two months’ time to comply with the directions vide
judgment dated 15.01.2020 by observing thus:
“9. Though we are not fully convinced with the reasons stated by the
appellants for delay in complying the directions in the judgment dated
15.01.2020, having considered the entire facts and circumstances, especially
the further steps stated as completed after the order dated 07.07.2025
passed by this Court extending the time for compliance of the judgment; as
a last chance , we are inclined to allow the above applications in part by
extending the time for complying with the directions contained in judgment
dated 15.01.2020 for a further period of two months from the date of this
order.”
3. The aforesaid two months’ time have lapsed long back, still the
respondent(s) is grouping in the dark and not complying with the orders of this
Court. The majesty of law cannot be allowed to be undermined by any person
howsoever high he or she may be. Hence, we refrain from expressing any
further opinion in this regard except granting liberty to the petitioner herein to
continue to prosecute the contempt proceedings before the High Court in
accordance with law. The jurisdictional High Court would be at liberty to
proceed to adjudicate the contempt proceedings and pass such further orders
as it deems fit in the facts and circumstances obtained in this case. Accordingly,
Special Leave Petition stands disposed of.
4. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The applicant - Kulvinder Singh was admitted to bail under
order of this Court dated 09.05.2017 subject to the following
conditions:
“(1)  The  petitioner  shall  not  leave  Bundi
(Rajasthan) where he resides.
(2) He shall report to the Kunadi Police Station,
Kota District, on every Monday.
(3) He shall not contact any witnesses nor make any
attempt to tamper with the evidence.”
2. The applicant has now prayed for deletion of Condition No. (2)
which requires the applicant to report to the Kunadi Police
1

--- Page 1170 ---
Station, Kota District on every Monday. It has been submitted that
the applicant suffers from blindness and, therefore, this condition
is highly onerous and the trial is yet to be concluded.
3. On 20.02.2026, we had issued notice to the respondents and
have required them to disclose the current status of the trial.
4. The learned counsel representing the respondent-State has
informed us that out of 48 witnesses only 3 have been examined thus
far. In such circumstances, we are of the view that the trial is
likely to take some more time to conclude.
5. In  such  circumstances,  we  are  of  the  opinion  that  the
Condition  No.  (2)  needs  to  be  deleted.  Accordingly,  IA  No.
24420/2026 and Miscellaneous Application are allowed.
6. Condition No. (2) as imposed in the order dated 09.05.2017
shall stand deleted.

We have heard Mr. Ranjit Kumar, learned Senior Counsel
appearing for the petitioners and Ms.Aishwarya Bhati, learned
Additional Solicitor General for respondent(s).
We have also perused the impugned judgment specifically
referring to condition No.2 in letter dated 17.01.2004.  The
view expressed by the High Court, in our view, does not warrant
1

--- Page 1174 ---
any interference as the said condition clearly states the manner
in which the petitioners are bound to make the offer.
The petitioners were fighting all along questioning the
very terms upon which t hey were given lease, which is inclusive
of 44% of the constructed part. It is for them to establish
which they intend to do so, suffice it to state that there is no
perversity in the ultimate conclusion arrived at by the High
Court.
In such view of the matter, the Special Leave Petition is
dismissed.
However, we make it clear that the impugned judgment and
order does not stand in the way of the petitioners approaching
the respondent(s) for appropriate modification of the terms of
the Agreement or seeking extension of lease period.
I.A. No. 291130/2026, for extension of lease period is
disposed of, accordingly. 
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

         UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R

settlement, the learned counsel for the parties submit that parties
were agreeable to a divorce by mutual consent and the only issue
